items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field
Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field; CPA, CMA, or other relevant professional credential
Minimum five years of progressively responsible experience in budgeting, financial planning and analysis, accounting, or a related financial management field
Demonstrated experience developing budgets, forecasts, financial models, and scenario or sensitivity analyses
Experience supervising, coaching, or leading professional staff
Experience in higher education or nonprofit financial management
Experience with Ellucian Colleague or a comparable enterprise resource planning (ERP) system
Experience with Synario, PFM, or comparable financial planning and scenario-modeling software

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the university’s annual operating and capital budget processes, including standardized timelines, assumptions, templates, review checkpoints, and departmental accountability.

Maximize the financial and budgeting capabilities of Ellucian Colleague to establish a consistent, integrated, and reliable university-wide budget process and improve budget entry, consolidation, monitoring, and reporting.
Develop and maintain institution-wide financial forecasts, with formal forecasts prepared at least quarterly and updated more frequently when material conditions change.

Prepare rolling revenue and expense projections and analyze key financial drivers, including enrollment, retention, tuition and fees, financial aid, compensation, benefits, and other operating assumptions.
Develop and document what-if scenarios, sensitivity analyses, and multi-year financial models to evaluate institutional priorities, financial sustainability, risks, and potential operating outcomes.

Become proficient in and effectively utilize the university’s scenario-planning/PFM software, including Synario as application, to support forecasting, scenario analysis, and long-range financial planning.

Prepare accurate, timely, and insightful budget-to-actual analyses, forecasts, dashboards, and financial reports for the CFO, President, Executive Leadership Team (ELT)/Cabinet, budget managers, and other university stakeholders.
Partner with the Controller to ensure budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning are grounded in accurate, reconciled, and timely financial results and clearly documented assumptions.

Collaborate regularly with Student Financial Services, Institutional Research, Advancement, Admissions, Academic Affairs, Human Resources, and other university offices to develop, validate, and communicate financial assumptions and projections.

Conduct financial assessments of proposed academic programs, staffing changes, capital investments, strategic initiatives, and other miscellaneous planning matters as requested by the CFO and university leadership.
Prepare financial analyses, business cases, and presentation materials for the CFO and President and, as requested, support presentations to the Finance Committee and other relevant Board committees.

Supervise, coach, and develop the Budget Analyst and an additional financial planning or analytical position as assigned; establish clear responsibilities, workflows, documentation standards, deadlines, cross-training, and quality expectations.
Support budget managers through financial guidance, training, and tools that promote consistent budgeting practices, fiscal responsibility, and informed decision-making across the university.
Maintain confidentiality of information regarding students, employees, donors, and institutional financial matters.
Responsible for supervising assigned staff including, but not limited to, hiring, training, evaluating, and managing performance.
Demonstrate a commitment to serving and inspiring students and colleagues in a context of a Christian University, integrating your Christian faith into your role and responsibilities.

Embrace the mission, vision , and values of Fresno Pacific University, affirm the FPU Faith Expectations (Download PDF reader) , and support the ideals and practices articulated in " The Fresno Pacific Idea ”
Uphold and advance Fresno Pacific University’s commitment to Christ-centered higher education, holistic student development, and serving diverse communities.
Complete tasks timely with work that is comprehensive, complete, and accurate
Communicates clearly, listens attentively, and seeks to understand others
Collaborates productively with colleagues of varying skillset
Other job duties as assigned
Indoors in a normal office environment with little exposure to excessive noise, dust, fumes, vibrations, and temperature changes at least eighty percent (80%) of the time.
Frequent computer use at a workstation, up to eight hours per day.
Frequently work at a fast pace with unscheduled interruptions.
Drive personal or University vehicles to appointments.
Public contact position requiring professional apparel, personal hygiene, and grooming.
This position typically functions indoors in an office environment with light to moderate noise associated with business office equipment. The position may involve travel for meetings and events.
Reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities will be provided in accordance with law.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and demonstrated ability to work with financial reporting, ERP, and analytical tools
Strong analytical, critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information for nonfinancial audiences
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills and demonstrated ability to collaborate across organizational functions
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, maintain confidentiality, and produce accurate work in a dynamic environment
Knowledge of higher education financial drivers, including enrollment, tuition, financial aid, and auxiliary or advancement revenue

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to: remain in a stationary position 80 % of the time, be able to move about inside the office to access file cabinets/office machinery etc., operate a computer and keyboard and other office productivity machinery such as calculators/copy machines/printers. The employee is occasionally required to position self to reach items on the floor and in high cabinetry.

The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 40 pounds. Employee must be able to communicate with others to exchange information including both over the telephone and in-person communication with callers and community members and be able to read a computer screen and paper documents.
